prose.text:
**Signals and interactions do not travel instantaneously.
There is an upper limit to their propagation speed.**

In special relativity, that limit is the vacuum light speed c, and every inertial frame measures the same vacuum light speed.
These laws require us to reexamine the ideas of space and time formed from everyday experience.

The classical idea of **absolute time** treats time as independent of matter and its motion, and as shared by all frames.
It is a useful approximation in many everyday low-speed situations, but not an exact and universal law of space and time.
prose.source_text: **认为信号和相互作用从一点传播到另一点是瞬时发生的****这种错误概念，是经典的空间和时间概念破产的原因. 相互作用的传递存在着极限终极速度，引起了改变以日常的实验为基础的空间和时间概念的必要性.** 永远跟物质和物质运动完全无关的用以确定速度流逝的**绝对时间**的概念，已是不正确的了.

prose.text:
First use the classical idea of absolute time and imagine that signals travel instantaneously, allowing direct comparison of event times at separated points $A$ and $B$.
This is a hypothetical assumption, not how real light signals propagate.

Place a clock at $A$ and another at $B$, both at rest in the same frame, and compare them using this imaginary signal.
For example, a signal leaves $A$ when its clock reads 0 hours 45 minutes.

If the signal reaches $B$ when the clock at $B$ reads that same time, the clocks are **synchronized**.
If their readings differ, advance the clock that is behind until the readings agree.
prose.source_text: 如果有信号的瞬间传播，那么在空间两个不同的点 $A$ 和$B$ 上两个事件同时发生的观点，将有绝对的意义. 可以在 $A$点和 $B$ 点上各放一个表，并用瞬间信号使它们同步. 如果一个信号由 $A$ 在 0 点 45 分发出，并且它传到 $B$ 点时也是在 $B$ 表这同一时刻，这就表明两个表指示的时间相同，即两表行走**同步**. 如果时间上不相符，则可把在信号发出时指示时间较慢的那个表拨快一点，以使两表同步.

prose.text:
In a chosen inertial frame, events such as lightning striking at two different places are simultaneous if the synchronized local clocks show the same time when the events occur.
We compare the local event times, not the times when the flashes reach someone's eyes.
prose.source_text: 任何两个事件，例如闪电的两次打击，如果它们在同步的两表指示的同一时刻发生的话，它们就是同时的.

prose.text:
Synchronized clocks at $A$ and $B$ let us compare local readings to decide whether events are simultaneous in that frame.
But real signals travel at a finite speed, so how can separated clocks be synchronized?
prose.source_text: 只有在 $A$ 点和 $B$ 点各放一个同步表才能判断在这两点上发生的两个事件是否同时. 但是，如果信号传播的速度不是无限大，那么怎样才能使互相间隔某距离的两表同步呢?

prose.text:
We can use light or other electromagnetic signals for synchronization because electromagnetic waves travel in vacuum at a definite constant speed c.
Every inertial frame measures the same vacuum light speed, and light traveling in opposite directions within that frame has the same speed.
prose.source_text: 要使两表同步，很自然地要采用光信号或电磁信号，因为电磁波在真空中的速度是严格确定的常量.

prose.text:
Radio time signals can be used to set a household clock to an accurate standard clock.
Knowing the distance from the radio station to the receiver and the propagation speed lets us calculate the signal's travel delay.

Clock-setting should allow for that delay, rather than treating reception as the instant of transmission.
The travel delay from a nearby station is often small enough to ignore in ordinary everyday clock-setting.
It cannot be ignored without considering the required precision, and signal travel time is especially important across large astronomical distances.
prose.source_text: 人们正是用这种方法用无线电来对表. 时间信号可以使你们的表和准确的标准钟同步. 已知道从无线电站到你家的距离，可以计算出信号耽误的时间. 这个耽误的时间肯定是非常小的. 在日常生活中，这点时间是不起什么重要作用的.但是，在极遥远的宇宙距离中，它就显得极其重要.

prose.text:
Figure 220 shows a synchronization method that uses symmetry without calculating the travel delay.
Imagine a spacecraft in uniform straight-line motion, with identical clocks $A$ and $B$ fixed at its ends.

A light source, at rest at the spacecraft's midpoint, emits a single flash.
In the spacecraft's inertial rest frame, the distances to the clocks are equal and light has the same speed in both directions.

The flash therefore reaches the clocks simultaneously.
If each clock shows the same time when the light arrives locally, the clocks are synchronized in this frame.
If the readings differ, one clock can be adjusted so that the two arrival events record the same time.
prose.source_text: 让我们较仔细地观察不需任何计算而使表同步的简单方法. 假设宇航员想知道放在宇宙飞船上两端的两个表 $A$ 和 $B$(图 220) 是否走得一样，那么他就得利用相对于飞船是静止的并且放在飞船中央的光源产生一次闪光. 光同时到达两个表. 如果此刻两表指示的时间相同，则两表同步.

prose.text: Figure 220
prose.label: 图 220

prose.text: Figure 221
prose.label: 图 221

prose.text:
The simultaneous arrivals above are defined in the spacecraft's inertial rest frame $K_1$.
In inertial frame $K$, which moves relative to the spacecraft, the craft's front moves away from the flash's emission location in the direction shown in Figure 221(a, b).

We are following the light after emission, not requiring the source to stay at its original location.
By the time light reaches the front clock $A$, it has traveled farther than half the spacecraft's length as measured in this frame.

The rear clock $B$ moves toward the emission location, so the light travels less than half that length to reach it.
Light travels at the vacuum speed c in both directions, so in $K$ it reaches the rear first and the front later.

The arrivals are not simultaneous.
This does not mean that clocks $A$ and $B$ have different ticking rates or are faulty.
It means that clocks synchronized in the craft's rest frame are not synchronized when compared using the other frame's synchronization rule.
prose.source_text: 但这只是对于与飞船相关的参考系 $K_1$ 而言的. 而在与飞船相对运动的参考系 $K$ 中情况就是另一种样子. 飞船头部的表要移动离开闪光源，光要到达表 $A$ 走过的距离就得大于半个飞船长度(图 221а, б). 反之，飞船尾上的表 $B$ 要移动靠近闪光地点，光信号的路程小于半个飞船的长度. 所以在 $K$系统上的观察者就会得出结论说，信号不是同时到达两表. 因此，表 $A$ 和表 $B$ 就走得不一样了.

prose.text:
In the example, points $A$ and $B$ are separated along the direction of relative motion.
The two light-arrival events are simultaneous in $K_1$ but not in $K$.

Thus **the simultaneity of spatially separated events depends on the chosen frame**.
A simultaneous pair in one frame is not necessarily simultaneous in all frames.

By the principle of relativity, inertial frames $K_1$ and $K$ are equivalent in their physical laws, with neither frame privileged.
Their simultaneity judgments can differ while each frame has a consistent definition of synchronization within itself.

This explanation uses both the finite propagation speed of signals and the postulate that all inertial frames have the same vacuum light speed c.
The finite speed of just any kind of signal is not enough by itself to establish this special-relativistic conclusion.
prose.source_text: 在 $A$ 点和 $B$ 点上的任何两个事件从 $K_1$ 系统的观察者角度来看是同时的，而从 $K$ 系统的观察者角度来看，又是不同时的. 但根据相对性原理，系统 $K_1$ 和系统 $K$ 完全是等效的，不能偏重其中任何一个系统. 所以我们不得不做出结论说，**由空间隔开的各事件的同时性是相对的.** 同时性的相对性的原因是，正如我们所见到的，信号传播速度的有限性.

prose.text:
Relative simultaneity resolves the apparent contradiction about the spherical light signal in Section 94.
At a single time in inertial frame $K$, light reaches the points of a sphere centered at $O$, so these arrival events are simultaneous in this frame.

In the relatively moving inertial frame $K_1$, that same set of arrival events is not all simultaneous.
Events at different positions along the direction of relative motion have different times.
The original set cannot be treated as the other frame's wavefront at a single time.
prose.source_text: 正是在同时性的相对性中蕴有解决第94节中提到的关于光的球面信号的矛盾的办法，只是从位于相对于系统$K$静止的观察者的角度来看，光同时到达以$O$为圆心的球形表面的各点.从与系统$K_1$相关的观察者的角度来看，光是在不同的时刻到达这些点上的.

prose.text:
Conversely, in inertial frame $K$, the other set of arrival events on a sphere centered at $O_1$ is not all simultaneous.
This set is simultaneous in inertial frame $K_1$, corresponding to the previous case with the frames exchanged.
Each frame's spherical wavefront is formed from positions at that frame's own common time, not at one universal instant.
prose.source_text: 可见，反过来说也是正确的：在系统$K$里光是在不同的时刻到达以$O_1$为中心的球的表面的各点，而不是同时到达的.这就正象在系统$K_1$里的观察者所看到的一样.

prose.text:
The descriptions of the spherical wavefronts are therefore consistent.
What must be abandoned is the classical assumption of a time shared by all inertial frames, not the common vacuum light speed in each frame.
prose.source_text: 由此可见，现实中任何不合常情的说法都是没有的.
